I respectfully disagree, this is a politically motivated work of fiction.

This video is full of false assumptions, logic based on those assumptions, and omissions.

First, it assumes that all individuals have the same IQ, the same profession, and have the same opportunity to earn. Even if all had the same characteristics, market and supply effects would result in differing wages, because the tax system is based on a capitalist economy, not a socialist or communist one.

It also assumes that that the progressive tax is based on earning and savings ("Tom saved money, Tom has more money"), when in fact the progressive system is based on earnings in a specific time frame. The saving tendencies of a individual affect their tax obligation very little.

Further, it assumes that taxing is based solely on governmental operating expenditures, which is false. If that was true, then there would be no tax break for married couples, and no break for "dependents" or children. These reductions in tax obligation are based on moral reasoning, not fiscal. These sort of tax breaks are social engineering incentives to tempt individuals to act in a certain fashion. If the tax code was based on only fiscal responsibility, there would only be controlled debt, and this country would either not have as large a government, or have a much higher tax rate.

The video also states that all three brother utilized the improvements equally. Bullshit. My guess is not many people in the bottom 50% of earning own road tractors or heavy equipment (which induces a much higher wear rate on roads), own manufacturing facilities (water / sewer utilities), have large tracks of land to develop (storm water management), have the same consumption (and therefore waste volume entering land fills) etc, etc, etc.

The progressive tax is not based on total income in the taxing period, it is based on income brackets in the taxing period. To simplify, assume there are three brackets - Bracket A: $0 - $25k, Bracket B: $25k - $75k, Bracket C: $75k and above. All three brothers would be taxed the same amount on the three brackets. All three would pay no tax on bracket A, 13% on bracket B, and 80% on bracket C. And for reference, the highest earning bracket currently is. 39.6% above $413k for the federal rate in 2015. Reference. The rates change per state for state taxes, but the brackets are the same, for the most part. The video does not cover this, leading the viewer to assume that a flat tax is assessed based on total earnings, which changes the conversation.

This video sets up a very particular situation to make a very board point, and to control the conversation regarding that broad point by pointing to injustices in that situation. It is a straw man argument, delivered by a skilled orientation, and is disingenuous at the very best.

I'm torn on this. Part of me commends what they are trying to achieve, and yet another part of me questions the logic of reverse engineering crap.

Actually, the basic architecture behind windows NT isn't bad ( the guy who designed VMS worked on it ), the problem is Microsoft has added so many cheap compatibility hacks over quick and dirty code and marketing horrors that the system never got a chance to shine.

ReactOS is more or less a NT compatible 'personality' for a generic kernel ( like the NT kernel is supposed to be ) with Wine running on top ( and a few drivers as a glue between the two ).
( To some extend, you could call it a basic OS for a windows port of Wine... )
So, no part of the UI is in kernel ( and other ugly hacks ) and the whole isn't a 1:1 translation but a rethinking from scratch that happen to be compatible.

So each part of the system is properly separated, and each can be debugged and tested more easely.

I think this is great because Windows XP is getting too old, and Windows 10 spies on you. I hope ReactOS ends up succeeding the windows family.

Can't wait to try it out.
